name: Arrokoth
type: Kuiper Belt Object · Cold-classical · Contact binary
fact: The most distant body ever visited by a spacecraft — 4.1 billion km from the Sun when New Horizons flew within 3,500 km on New Year's Day 2019. Its two lobes (Wenu and Weeyo) gently merged at the dawn of the solar system and have stayed merged for 4.5 billion years at ~40 K.
bio: Discovered in 2014 by Hubble and originally catalogued as 2014 MU69. Renamed Arrokoth (Powhatan for 'sky') in 2019 after the New Horizons flyby — a pristine remnant of the planetesimal disk preserved unmodified since formation. Its red, gently-accreted contact-binary shape is a direct fingerprint of how planet-building started in the outer solar system.
